extraction.name: RoboFAC dataset
extraction.description: RoboFAC is a large-scale dataset for question-answering on robot failure videos, comprising 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments. It covers six types of robotic failures organized across three hierarchical levels (task planning, motion planning, and execution control), with eight question types targeting task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu; Minghao Ye; Zewei Ye; Ruihan Tao; Shuo Yang; Bo Zhao
extraction.citeAs: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao. RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction. arXiv:2505.12224, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Simulation data was collected for 14 robotic tasks in the ManiSkill environment, augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. Expert policies were defined by specifying target end-effector poses, and failure data was generated by replacing expert policies with code snippets that produce erroneous trajectories. Real-world data for 6 tasks was collected via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm. Each video was recorded along with a corresponding descriptive text capturing the substage of failure, failure taxonomy, and error details.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection; Software Collection; Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Motion planning for the robotic arm occasionally failed, resulting in trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions; approximately 25% of collected simulation data was discarded during manual data cleaning.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Robotic failure and success videos from the ManiSkill simulation environment augmented with YCB Object Dataset objects and ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR scenes; real-world teleoperation videos from the SO-100 robotic arm; each video accompanied by a descriptive text file containing substage information, failure taxonomy, error details, and perturbed end-effector poses.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For five question types (task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, failure locating), reference answers were directly extracted from textual descriptions collected during video recording. For the remaining three types (failure explanation, high-level correction, low-level correction), GPT-4o was used to generate reference answers using the video and its textual description as inputs. All GPT-4o outputs were manually reviewed and corrected by human annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All outputs generated by GPT-4o were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current integration of the RoboFAC model into the VLA-controlled robotic system is not yet seamless; the model is applied exclusively to the VLA model and not to hierarchical policies; success rate in real-world tasks remains subject to further enhancement due to the VLA model's limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions; approximately 25% of simulation data was discarded during manual cleaning due to motion planning failures resulting in trajectories misaligned with textual descriptions
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of multimodal large language models for robotic failure analysis and correction; benchmarking model capabilities in task understanding, failure detection, failure identification, failure locating, failure explanation, and failure correction based on robot manipulation videos; integration as an external critic in real-world VLA robotic control pipelines to provide recovery suggestions
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To generate failure data in simulation, the original expert policy was replaced with a code snippet that generates an erroneous trajectory at a selected substage, causing the overall robotic task to fail. Perturbations were introduced to end-effector poses to create position deviation and orientation deviation failures. The dataset also includes successful trajectories collected alongside failure trajectories to prevent models from overfitting to failure patterns. For the real-world data, failures were collected via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm. For annotation of failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction question types, GPT-4o was used to generate reference answers based on video and textual descriptions, with all outputs manually reviewed and corrected.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Given the motion planning for the robotic arm occasionally failed, resulting in trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions, the authors manually performed thorough data cleaning and retained approximately 75% of the collected simulation data. All outputs from GPT-4o used for annotation were manually reviewed and corrected.
